definitions.explanation: A heraldic symbol used to identify a Japanese family, clan, or organization. Traditionally displayed on formal kimono, gates, and household items. Similar in function to European coats of arms.
A decorative pattern or natural marking, such as the pattern on an animal's body or a design motif.

examples.english: Our family crest is a chrysanthemum.

examples.japanese: ⟦{着物|きもの}→着物：01309_kimono⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{家紋|かもん}→家紋：15366_kamon⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{入|はい}っている→入る：00494_hairu⟧。
examples.english: The kimono has a family crest on it.

examples.japanese: {徳川家|とくがわけ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{紋|もん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{三|み}つ{葉|ば}→三つ葉：11242_mitsuba⟧{葵|あおい}⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{広|ひろ}く→広い：00704_hiroi⟧⟦{知|し}られている→知る：00458_shiru⟧。
examples.english: The Tokugawa family crest is widely known as the triple hollyhock.

examples.english: Each person has a unique fingerprint.
Tigers have distinctive stripe patterns on their bodies.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
Japanese family crests (⟦{家紋|かもん}→家紋：15366_kamon⟧) date back to the Heian period and became widespread among samurai families. Today, most Japanese families have a ⟦{家紋|かもん}→家紋：15366_kamon⟧, though many people are unaware of theirs. The imperial family uses the ⟦{菊|きく}→菊：15342_kiku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{御紋|ごもん} (chrysanthemum crest), and it remains a symbol of the Japanese government.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{家紋|かもん}→家紋：15366_kamon⟧: family crest
- ⟦{紋付|もんつき}→紋付：06294_montsuki⟧: crested formal kimono
- ⟦{菊|きく}→菊：15342_kiku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{紋|もん}: chrysanthemum crest
- ⟦{指紋|しもん}→指紋：12728_shimon⟧: fingerprint
- {紋|もん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{入|はい}る→入る：00494_hairu⟧: have a crest on it
